seoul.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
seoul.text: The main palace of the Joseon dynasty, first built in 1395. Arrive for the changing of the guard at Gwanghwamun gate, then walk through to Gyeonghoeru, the pavilion on the pond. It is closed on Tuesdays, and entry is free if you wear hanbok.

seoul.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
seoul.text: Lanes of traditional tiled-roof houses on the hill between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung. People live here, so keep your voice down; the busiest residential lanes are open to visitors only during daytime hours.

seoul.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
seoul.text: A restored stream that runs for nearly 11 kilometres through the centre, a few steps below street level. It is at its best in the evening: start at Cheonggye Plaza near Gwanghwamun and walk east towards Gwangjang Market.

seoul.name: Gwangjang Market
seoul.text: One of Seoul's oldest covered markets and the easiest place to try market food: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap and knife-cut noodles, eaten at the stall's bench.

seoul.name: Myeongdong
seoul.text: Seoul's best-known shopping streets for cosmetics and fashion. Street food stalls set up from late afternoon, and Myeongdong Cathedral at the top of the hill is a quiet break from the crowds.

seoul.name: N Seoul Tower on Namsan
seoul.text: The tower on the hill in the middle of the city. Take the cable car or the Namsan circular bus, or walk up through the park in about 30 to 40 minutes, and time it for sunset.

busan.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
busan.text: A temple built on the rocks above the sea, north-east of Haeundae, which is rare in a country where most temples are in the mountains. Go early in the morning, before the tour buses, and expect a lot of steps.

busan.name: Haeundae Beach and Blueline Park
busan.text: Busan's most famous beach. From Mipo, at its eastern end, small sky capsules and a beach train run along the old coastal railway to Cheongsapo and Songjeong; book ahead at weekends.

busan.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
busan.text: Brightly painted houses stacked up a steep hillside, with murals, small galleries and viewpoints. Take the village bus or a taxi up from Toseong Station and walk down.

busan.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
busan.text: Korea's largest seafood market. Choose your fish from the tanks on the ground floor and have it prepared in the restaurants upstairs; BIFF Square and Gukje Market are a short walk away.

busan.name: Gwangalli Beach
busan.text: The beach with the view of Gwangan Bridge, which is lit up after dark. Cafés and bars line the seafront, and a drone light show is held on many Saturday evenings.

busan.name: Spa Land Centum City
busan.text: A large, modern jjimjilbang inside the Shinsegae Centum City department store, with hot spring baths and many themed sauna rooms. It is an easy first Korean bathhouse.

jeju.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
jeju.text: A volcanic crater rising out of the sea on the east coast. The stair climb to the rim takes 20 to 30 minutes, and sunrise is the classic time to go. Udo island is a short ferry ride from the nearby port.

jeju.name: Hyeopjae Beach
jeju.text: White sand, black lava rock and shallow turquoise water on the west coast, with the small island of Biyangdo straight ahead. Hallim Park is across the road.

jeju.name: Hamdeok Beach
jeju.text: A wide, pale beach about 30 minutes east of Jeju City, with a short walk up Seoubong hill for the view. It is easy to reach by bus, and good even in winter, when the sea turns a milky green.

jeju.name: Hallasan
jeju.text: South Korea's highest mountain at 1,947 metres. The two summit trails, Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa, need a free advance reservation and an early start; Eorimok and Yeongsil are shorter and reach the high plateau but not the crater.

jeju.name: Jeju Five-Day Market
jeju.text: A big traditional market near the airport, held on dates ending in 2 and 7. Come for tangerines, dried fish, street snacks and a look at everyday island life.

jeju.name: Arte Museum Jeju
jeju.text: A large immersive media art space in Aewol, with rooms of projected waves, flowers and waterfalls. It is a useful plan for a rainy or very windy day.

gyeongju.name: Bulguksa Temple
gyeongju.text: A UNESCO-listed temple from the Silla kingdom, known for its stone staircases and the two pagodas in the main courtyard, Dabotap and Seokgatap. Seokguram grotto is further up the mountain by shuttle bus or a forest path.

gyeongju.name: Daereungwon Tomb Complex
gyeongju.text: A park of grassy royal burial mounds in the middle of town. You can walk inside one of them, Cheonmachong, to see how a Silla tomb was built.

gyeongju.name: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond
gyeongju.text: The site of a Silla palace garden, best visited just after dark, when the rebuilt pavilions are lit and reflected in the pond.

gyeongju.name: Woljeonggyo Bridge
gyeongju.text: A grand covered wooden bridge, rebuilt on its Silla-era site beside the Gyochon hanok village. It is free to cross and beautifully lit at night.

gyeongju.name: Hwangnidan-gil
gyeongju.text: The street beside the tomb park where old hanok houses have become cafés, restaurants and small shops. This is where to try Gyeongju bread and ten-won bread.

jeonju.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
jeonju.text: Hundreds of traditional houses in one district, many of them guesthouses, tea rooms and craft shops. Renting hanbok for a few hours is popular here, and the lanes are prettiest early in the morning and after dark.

jeonju.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine
jeonju.text: A shrine built in 1410 to hold the portrait of King Taejo, founder of the Joseon dynasty, with a small bamboo grove inside the walls.

jeonju.name: Jeondong Cathedral
jeonju.text: A red-brick Catholic cathedral from the early 1900s, directly opposite Gyeonggijeon and one of the most photographed buildings in the city.

jeonju.name: Omokdae
jeonju.text: A pavilion on a low hill at the edge of the hanok village. A ten-minute climb gives you the view over all the tiled roofs.

jeonju.name: Nambu Market
jeonju.text: The old market just south of the village, known for kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout soup with rice) in the morning and a night market on weekend evenings.

gangneung.name: Ojukheon
gangneung.text: The birthplace of the scholar Yi I and his mother, the artist Shin Saimdang, who appear on the 5,000 and 50,000 won notes. The house is named after the black bamboo that grows around it.

gangneung.name: Gyeongpo Beach and Lake
gangneung.text: A long sandy beach with a lagoon just behind it. A flat path circles the lake, lined with cherry trees in April, and Gyeongpodae pavilion looks over the water.

gangneung.name: Anmok Coffee Street
gangneung.text: A row of cafés facing the sea at Anmok Beach, the heart of Gangneung's reputation as Korea's coffee city. Take a window seat upstairs.

gangneung.name: Jeongdongjin
gangneung.text: A small seaside village south of the city with a railway station right on the beach, famous as a sunrise spot, especially on New Year's Day.

gangneung.name: Arte Museum Gangneung
gangneung.text: An immersive media art museum near Gyeongpo Lake, with themes drawn from the mountains and sea of Gangwon. A good plan for a rainy day.

incheon.name: Incheon Chinatown
incheon.text: Korea's oldest Chinatown, at the end of subway Line 1, and the home of jjajangmyeon. The painted Fairy Tale Village and Jayu Park are next door.

incheon.name: Songdo Central Park
incheon.text: A park built around a seawater canal in the new city of Songdo, surrounded by glass towers. You can rent small boats, and the skyline is at its best around sunset.

incheon.name: Wolmido
incheon.text: A seafront promenade with fairground rides, seafood restaurants and ferries, a short bus or monorail ride from Incheon Station.

incheon.name: Incheon Grand Park
incheon.text: A very large city park with a lake, an arboretum and bike rental, known for its cherry blossom tunnel in April and its autumn leaves.

sokcho.name: Seoraksan National Park
sokcho.text: The granite peaks behind the town. From the main Sogongwon entrance, a cable car goes up to Gwongeumseong for wide views with very little walking, and trails lead to Ulsanbawi rock and Biryong Falls.

sokcho.name: Biseondae
sokcho.text: A broad rock terrace beside a clear stream in Cheonbuldong Valley, reached by a mostly gentle walk of about an hour from the Sogongwon entrance. Despite the English name sometimes used, it is not a summit.

sokcho.name: Yeonggeumjeong
sokcho.text: A pavilion on the rocks at the edge of Dongmyeong Port, reached by a short bridge over the waves. It is one of the easiest sunrise spots on the east coast.

sokcho.name: Sokcho Tourist and Fishery Market
sokcho.text: The central market, also called Jungang Market, where queues form for boxes of dakgangjeong (sweet crispy chicken), and for fresh and dried seafood.

sokcho.name: Abai Village
sokcho.text: A neighbourhood settled by refugees from the North during the Korean War. Cross on the gaetbae, a small ferry pulled by hand along a cable, and try squid sundae.

sokcho.name: Naksansa Temple
sokcho.text: A temple on a sea cliff in Yangyang, about 20 minutes south of Sokcho. Walk out to the Hongryeonam hermitage above the waves and up to the tall statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion.

yeosu.name: Hyangiram Hermitage
yeosu.text: A small hermitage on the cliffs at the tip of Dolsan island, its name meaning "facing the sun". The climb from the village takes 20 to 30 minutes, through narrow gaps between boulders, and it is a famous place to watch the sunrise.

yeosu.name: Odongdo Island
yeosu.text: A small wooded island joined to the city by a long breakwater. Its camellias flower from late winter into early spring, and a path leads to a lighthouse and sea cliffs.

yeosu.name: Yeosu Maritime Cable Car
yeosu.text: A cable car across the harbour between Dolsan Park and Jasan Park, with glass-floored cabins if you want them. Ride it around dusk for the lights.

yeosu.name: Jongpo Marine Park
yeosu.text: The waterfront promenade where Yeosu's well-known night sea is at its liveliest, with buskers, street food stalls and views of the bridges.

yeosu.name: Yi Sun-sin Square
yeosu.text: The central square by the old harbour, with a replica of a turtle ship beside it. Admiral Yi Sun-sin's navy was based in Yeosu during the wars of the 1590s.

daegu.name: Seomun Market
daegu.text: One of the biggest traditional markets in Korea, known for fabric and for its food alleys: flat dumplings (napjak mandu) and knife-cut noodles. A night market runs in the warmer months.

daegu.name: Kim Gwang-seok Street
daegu.text: A lane of murals, music and small cafés dedicated to a much-loved folk singer who grew up nearby, beside Bangcheon Market.

daegu.name: Cheongna Hill and the Modern History Alley
daegu.text: Missionary houses from the early 1900s, the 90 steps of the March First Movement and Gyesan Cathedral, linked by an easy signposted walk through the old town.

daegu.name: Apsan Observatory
daegu.text: A viewpoint over the whole city, reached by cable car and a short walk. Go just before sunset and stay for the lights.

daegu.name: Donghwasa Temple
daegu.text: A large temple on Palgongsan, north of the city, with a towering stone Buddha. A cable car nearby climbs higher up the mountain.

daejeon.name: Hanbat Arboretum
daejeon.text: A large, free garden in the middle of the city, next to the Expo site and the art museums. It is an easy place for a slow walk in spring and autumn.

daejeon.name: National Science Museum
daejeon.text: Korea's main science museum, with hands-on halls that work well with children. Much of it is free or low-cost.

daejeon.name: Sungsimdang Bakery
daejeon.text: The bakery, founded in 1956, that Koreans travel to Daejeon for. The main shop is near Jungangno Station; expect a queue for the fried soboro bread.

daejeon.name: Yuseong Hot Springs Foot Bath
daejeon.text: A free outdoor foot bath fed by hot spring water in the Yuseong district. Bring a small towel.

daejeon.name: Gyejoksan Red Clay Trail
daejeon.text: A forest trail covered in soft red clay and made for walking barefoot, with places to wash your feet afterwards.

gwangju.name: Asia Culture Center and May 18 Democracy Square
gwangju.text: A large arts complex built around the square and the former provincial office at the centre of the May 1980 uprising. Exhibitions change often, and the grounds are pleasant in the evening.

gwangju.name: May 18th National Cemetery
gwangju.text: The memorial and resting place of those who died in the 1980 democratic uprising, north of the city, with a small exhibition hall. A quiet, moving visit.

gwangju.name: Yangnim-dong and Penguin Village
gwangju.text: A neighbourhood of early 20th-century missionary houses and hanok, plus an alley decorated by residents with clocks, pots and old signs.

gwangju.name: Mudeungsan National Park
gwangju.text: The mountain on the edge of the city, known for its columns of volcanic rock near the top. The walk to Jeungsimsa temple is an easy introduction.

gwangju.name: Juknokwon Bamboo Forest, Damyang
gwangju.text: Walking paths through a dense bamboo grove in the next county, about 40 minutes away by bus, near the tree-lined Metasequoia Road.
